title: sein — the verb to be
objective: Use the correct present-tense form of sein (bin, bist, ist, sind) to describe yourself and others.
explanation: "Sein" (to be) is the most essential German verb. Its present-tense forms are irregular: ich bin (I am), du bist (you are), er/sie/es ist (he/she/it is), wir/sie/Sie sind (we/they/you-formal are). Compare Danish: Danish uses one form "er" for all persons. German keeps a separate form for each person, so you must match the verb to the subject each time.
sourceReference: Teacher-authored example. Conjugation verified against standard German grammar reference (sein, Präsens).

exercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the form of "sein" for "she"?
exercises.feedbackCorrect: Correct. "Sie ist" — "ist" is the third-person singular form of sein.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: For "sie" (she), the form of sein is "ist": "Sie ist Lehrerin." — "bin" is only for "ich", and "bist" only for "du".
With "ich" (I), the form of sein is always "bin": "Ich bin Studentin."

exercises.prompt: Write two German sentences: one about yourself and one about another person, using the correct form of sein each time.
